english.title: Repair a hallmarked article without written consent of an assay office
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), made a repair to an article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), bearing approved hallmarks otherwise in accordance with the written consent of an assay office
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1) of and Schedule 3 to the Hallmarking Act 1973.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 10 of the Hallmarking Act 1973 allows the court, following conviction, to order any article the subject of the proceedings to be delivered to an assay office who, (subject to the order), may exercise the like powers under this Act in relation to the article as if it had been submitted to them for hallmarking.
(ii) The time limit on prosecutions is three years from the commission of the offence or one year from its discovery by the prosecutor whichever is the earlier (Para. 2 of Schedule 3).

Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
